newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's Kiet calls for Hanoi-Saigon freeway plan.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's Kiet calls for Hanoi-Saigon freeway plan.

text.p: Vietnamese Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has called for work to start on a feasibility study to build a freeway linking Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, a Ministry of Transport and Communication official said on Monday.
He said construction of the 1,800-km (1,125-mile) express road between the capital and the former Saigon, the country's economic hub, would start in 1998 after a one-year study.
The cost of the project has been estimated at $6 billion, equivalent to more than a quarter of the country's annual national income.
"The problem is money, not the capacity," said an official at the Transport Design consulting company, which is working on a master plan for the road.
"If we have enough money it will take just about two to three years to complete," he said. "If not, the construction might last for 10 years, it depends."
More than $500 million has already been earmarked for a revamp of Highway One, the flood-prone and potholed main road which runs between the country's two main cities.
